name: CircuitBreaker
purpose: Short-circuit calls to a failing dependency by transitioning between closed, open, and half-open states driven by a rolling failure metric.
api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Awaitable, Callable, TypeVar, Literal

T = TypeVar('T')
State = Literal['closed', 'open', 'half_open']

class CircuitBreaker(Protocol):
    name: str
    state: State
    async def call(self, fn: Callable[..., Awaitable[T]], /, *args, **kwargs) -> T: ...
    def on_success(self, elapsed_ms: float) -> None: ...
    def on_failure(self, exc: BaseException, elapsed_ms: float) -> None: ...
    def force_open(self, reason: str) -> None: ...
    def allow_probe(self) -> bool: ...
invariants: When state is open the breaker MUST reject calls without invoking the wrapped function.
The transition from open to half-open SHALL occur only after the configured cooldown interval has elapsed.
A half-open breaker MUST permit at most the configured permitted_calls_in_half_open probes concurrently.
A single failure recorded while half-open SHALL force the state back to open and restart the cooldown.
The breaker CANNOT make a transition decision using a sample smaller than minimum_number_of_calls.
The breaker NEVER mutates state without emitting a state_transition event on the observability bus.
extension_contract: Adopters register a FailureClassifier provider that decides which exceptions count as failures, slow_call_duration_threshold, and a state listener hook; the sliding window type (count-based or time-based) is selected via a SlidingWindowPolicy adapter. Rolling metrics and the state machine itself remain sealed.

sources.source: Nygard, Release It! 2nd edition (2018), Pragmatic Bookshelf

why_essential: Without a shared breaker every caller reinvents its own failure-detection loop, creating inconsistent thresholds, divergent cooldowns and thundering-herd recovery storms against a convalescing dependency.
alternatives_considered: Per-call timeout only: detects slowness but NEVER stops the caller from piling load onto a sick dependency.
Retry with exponential backoff alone: amplifies load during outages instead of shedding it.
Client-side rate limiter: caps throughput but cannot react to the dependency's actual health signals.
